weights.csoNote: Uganda: stroke is often YOUNGER than Western data, with RHD/AF cardioembolism and HIV-associated mechanisms prominent. CRITICAL: ischaemic vs haemorrhagic CANNOT be distinguished clinically — CT is required but often unavailable; this changes management. Always CHECK GLUCOSE first (hypoglycaemia mimics stroke — DEFG).
weights.weightCitation: AHA/ASA 2019 Acute Ischemic Stroke Guidelines (Powers WJ et al., Stroke 2019); WHO; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Uganda: hypertensive intracerebral haemorrhage is proportionally MORE common than in Western data (high uncontrolled-hypertension burden). Cannot be distinguished from ischaemic stroke without CT. Headache/vomiting/reduced consciousness favour haemorrhage but are not reliable. Reverse anticoagulation urgently if present.
weights.weightCitation: AHA/ASA 2022 Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage Guideline (Greenberg SM et al., Stroke 2022); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Presents more as thunderclap HEADACHE than focal weakness, but a sentinel bleed/complication can give focal signs. CT then LP (xanthochromia).
weights.weightCitation: AHA/ASA aneurysmal SAH guidance; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL must-not-miss (pin on diabetes / insulin-sulfonylurea). Dominant trigger is the GLUCOSE VALUE (vitals; also via vitals-escalation pack). DEFG — ALWAYS check capillary glucose in ANY focal deficit before calling it a stroke; hypoglycaemia can produce focal signs that fully reverse with glucose. Sulfonylureas cause prolonged/recurrent hypoglycaemia.
weights.weightCitation: ADA Standards of Care 2024 (hypoglycaemia); Davidson's 24th ed (hypoglycaemia as a stroke mimic — DEFG)

weights.csoNote: Subacute progressive focal deficit +/- seizures +/- raised-ICP headache. Uganda: in HIV consider toxoplasmosis, tuberculoma, primary CNS lymphoma (see those entries); also metastases and primary tumours.
Transient focal deficit AFTER a witnessed seizure, resolving over minutes-hours — but a first seizure with focal deficit still needs imaging to exclude an underlying lesion.

LMN facial palsy with FOREHEAD INVOLVED (cannot wrinkle/close eye) distinguishes it from UMN (stroke) facial palsy where the forehead is spared. Uganda: HIV can cause Bell's palsy and other cranial neuropathies; exclude herpes zoster oticus / parotid lesion.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's 24th ed (Bell's palsy — LMN facial nerve, forehead involved)

weights.csoNote: A TIA is a 'brain attack' WARNING — high early stroke risk, must not be dismissed (urgent secondary prevention; ABCD2). KEY GAP: the defining feature — full RESOLUTION of the deficit (<24h) — is NOT a capture token; without a 'transient/resolved deficit' field the EMR cannot separate TIA from an evolving stroke. Recommend adding one.
weights.weightCitation: AHA/ASA TIA definition & management (ABCD2); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Overlaps 'Acute ischaemic stroke' but flags the distinct mechanisms (and different WORKUP) that dominate stroke in YOUNGER Ugandans: HIV vasculopathy, RHD cardioembolism, vasculitis, sickle-cell, hypercoagulable states. Prompts HIV test, echo, vasculitis/thrombophilia screen. 'young' threshold is an extrapolation — confirm with CSO.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's 24th ed; stroke-in-HIV / young-stroke literature (HIV vasculopathy, RHD cardioembolism, vasculitis, hypercoagulable states)

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL must-not-miss (pin on HIV/immunosuppression). basePrior population-dependent — the commonest FOCAL brain lesion in advanced HIV (CD4<100) in Uganda. Subacute focal deficit/seizures + multiple ring-enhancing lesions on CT; empirical anti-toxoplasma trial; differential is tuberculoma / primary CNS lymphoma.
weights.weightCitation: WHO HIV/opportunistic-infection guidelines; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL must-not-miss (pin on TB/HIV exposure). Uganda: given the very high TB burden, intracranial tuberculoma is an important focal mass lesion — subacute focal deficit/seizures +/- constitutional TB features. A key differential of CNS toxoplasmosis in HIV; often coexists with TB meningitis. basePrior under-characterised locally — confirm with CSO.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on TB; Uganda National TB & Leprosy Programme; Davidson's 24th ed (tuberculoma)

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on FEVER (cerebral malaria without fever is essentially never). Cerebral malaria USUALLY causes DIFFUSE encephalopathy (coma, seizures) rather than classic focal hemiparesis — focal signs/post-malaria neurological syndromes are less typical. In holoendemic Uganda, any febrile neuro presentation needs a malaria RDT/smear; check glucose (DEFG); exclude concurrent meningitis.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Guidelines for Malaria (2025); Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Predominantly a SEIZURE disorder (overlaps Todd's paresis) rather than primary focal weakness; focal deficits less common. Uganda: a leading cause of adult-onset seizures in pig-keeping areas (Taenia solium). The pork/Taenia exposure is not specifically tokenised ('high-risk exposure' is the proxy). Calcified/cystic lesions on CT.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's 24th ed; WHO Taenia solium / neurocysticercosis guidance

weights.csoNote: THE must-not-miss NON-STROKE cause of limb weakness — unconditional. Distinguished from stroke by a pattern the tokens capture poorly: BILATERAL LEG weakness (paraparesis), a SENSORY LEVEL, back pain, and bladder/bowel involvement (only 'incontinence' is tokenised). Strong NEGATIVE weights on stroke-pattern tokens. Uganda: Pott's (spinal TB) and malignant compression are key — a SENSORY LEVEL demands urgent MRI + decompression/steroids; do not mislabel as stroke. (Recommend 'sensory level' + 'paraparesis' tokens.)
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's 24th ed (spinal cord compression — malignant, and tuberculous/Pott's)

weights.csoNote: DIAGNOSIS OF EXCLUSION made on POSITIVE signs (Hoover's, give-way weakness, inconsistency) — NOT merely the absence of a lesion, and NOT before excluding stroke/cord/structural causes and checking glucose. The positive functional signs are examination findings not in the token set. The engine must never rank this above an unexcluded must-not-miss.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's 24th ed (functional/dissociative neurological disorder — positive signs e.g. Hoover's)
